statusText: Mapped policy state: WATCH. Broad U.S. equity weakness, negative Nasdaq breadth, Brent near $108 and a roughly 5% 10-year Treasury yield keep pressure aligned, while stronger chip shares and unavailable direct NQ retracement-quality evidence limit Tail below elevated.
recommendation: Mapped policy state: WATCH. Tail remains below the elevated threshold; a higher band would require verified persistent NQ extension, shallow pullbacks, failed retracements or session-extreme holding.
headline: Broad weakness and oil-rate pressure keep Tail in WATCH; Stress remains extreme
body: AP reported at 12:52 p.m. ET that the Nasdaq Composite was down 0.7%, the 10-year Treasury yield was about 4.99% and Brent was near $108.12. Nvidia and AMD were higher, creating a technology-sector conflict signal. Direct current NQ pullback and extension structure was not independently available.

lookbackSummary: Across the prior 24 UTC clock-hours, Tail ranged from 18% to 22%. It was mostly low overnight, returned to WATCH through much of Tuesday morning, briefly eased around the U.S. open, and moved back into WATCH as broad U.S. weakness persisted.
outlookSummary: Current Tail is in WATCH as broad equity weakness, high oil and near-5% Treasury yields sustain extreme Stress, but direct no-retracement NQ evidence remains unavailable and chip shares are firmer. Power hour is the nearest conditional danger window; Wednesday's 12:30 UTC data, cash open and later FOMC sequence keep forward Stress high.

forecast.analysis: AP had Nasdaq -0.7% at 12:52 ET, 10Y near 4.99% and Brent near $108.12. Chip shares were firmer; direct NQ retracement evidence was unavailable, keeping Tail in WATCH.
drivers: Nasdaq weakness with 10Y near 5% and Brent near $108
Chip strength and missing direct NQ path evidence cap Tail

forecast.analysis: If early-afternoon losses stabilize with meaningful rebounds, Tail stays at the WATCH floor; failed rebounds with fresh extension would raise path risk.
Power hour through the 20:00 UTC close is the main danger window. Session-low holding after failed rebounds would lift path risk; a broad retracement would not.
After the cash close, Tail falls to low if after-hours trade retraces normally. Continued extension without meaningful pullbacks would invalidate that path.
If early after-hours trade is orderly, Tail stays low. A fresh energy or geopolitical shock would need sustained NQ follow-through to change the path assessment.
drivers: Fresh shocks require sustained NQ follow-through

forecast.analysis: Evening Tail stays low if price discovery remains balanced. Repeated cross-asset extension, not a brief headline move, would be the escalation signal.
Late-evening Tail stays low if trading remains two-sided. A persistent break with shallow pullbacks would be the contrary path.
During the Asia transition, Tail stays low if price discovery is two-sided. A break that holds with shallow pullbacks would raise path risk.
If Asia remains orderly, Tail stays low as Stress eases modestly. Cross-asset alignment matters only if NQ also develops persistent extension.
Quieter overnight trade keeps Tail low if retracements remain available. Repeated failed pullbacks would be the main invalidation.
As Asia matures, transition uncertainty rises slightly without implying trend. Persistent direction across regional handoffs would raise Tail.
At the Europe transition, low Tail assumes a rotational handoff. Rates and oil become stronger amplifiers only with shallow NQ pullbacks.
European trade keeps Tail low if no persistent NQ leg develops. A failed retracement followed by extension would be the contrary pattern.
Approaching U.S. premarket participation, Tail remains low if futures stay two-sided. Persistent direction would narrow the margin to WATCH.
Premarket Tail stays low if overnight direction gets meaningful retracement. Aligned rates, oil and megacaps could amplify a persistent move.
The pre-data setup stays below WATCH if markets remain two-sided. Stress remains extreme because major U.S. checkpoints follow later Wednesday.
drivers: Event density raises Stress before Tail

forecast.analysis: WATCH begins as the 12:30 UTC data window nears. Scheduled events raise Stress, but Tail still depends on observed post-release persistence.
drivers: Retail Sales and import/export prices at 12:30 UTC

forecast.analysis: About two hours before the releases, Tail stays at the WATCH floor. A higher band still depends on later observed price-path persistence.
drivers: Event proximity raises Stress more than Tail

forecast.analysis: In the final full pre-release hour, WATCH reflects compressed event risk. Escalation requires the later reaction to persist with poor retracement.
This hour contains the 12:30 UTC releases. Tail rises conditionally only if the reaction persists with shallow pullbacks or failed retracements.
The 13:30 UTC U.S. cash open follows the data. Tail reaches 24% only conditionally if opening direction persists with shallow pullbacks.
The first full cash hour remains WATCH conditionally. Repeated extension after failed retracements sustains path risk; rotation reduces it.
Tail sits at the WATCH floor if post-open trade remains unsettled. A settled two-sided range lowers path risk; renewed extension sustains WATCH.
If meaningful afternoon retracement develops, Tail falls to low. The 18:00 UTC FOMC decision remains a later Stress checkpoint, not an assumed reaction.

forecastDetail.comment: Current broad equity weakness and oil/rate pressure support WATCH, while chip strength and missing direct NQ retracement evidence cap Tail below elevated.
Early-afternoon stabilization would keep Tail near the WATCH floor; failed rebounds followed by extension would be the contrary signal.
Power hour through the cash close is the main danger window; session-low holding after failed rebounds would strengthen one-way-path risk.
Post-close Tail falls to low if after-hours trade shows ordinary retracement; continued extension without pullbacks would invalidate that path.
Early after-hours Tail stays low if trade remains orderly; fresh shocks would need sustained NQ follow-through to change the assessment.
Evening Tail stays low if price discovery remains balanced; repeated cross-asset extension would be the contrary signal.
